messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate in region az3 detected by synthetic probes. 90th latency also creeping up. Rolling window: 2m. Provisional severity: SEV2.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident #PID-83421 triggered and routed to oncall (alex.chen). Paging sequence started.
alex.chen: acked. I'm on it. grabbing console + logs. anyone seeing customer-facing pages?
mira: seeing spikes on metric dashboards too. Per-route error rate: gen-text-v2 ~12% 5xx over 1m. Other models lower but trending.
jordan: confirmed. Batches backlog increasing on az3 serving pool, mean queue depth x6.
sasha: adding: autoscaler hasn't kicked for some of the dedicated pools (az3-dedicated-1). Possible orchestration delay.
alex.chen: thanks. mira — can you post the short graph of error vs qdepth?
mira: pasted snapshot link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/az3/az3-overview?panel=5 (short lived)
ops-coordinator: Noted. I'm preparing customer-impact snippet for status page. Celine, heads-up for SRM.
celine-srm: on it. I'll message impacted accounts once we have confirmed degradation and ETA.
alex.chen: quick triage steps: 1) check node-level health 2) check proxy/sidecar logs for 502/524 patterns 3) see if model shard eviction or OOMs. I'll run the first two.
jordan: running: `kubectl get pods -n serving -l region=az3 -o wide`
```
NAME                                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
serving-az3-rt-0                       1/1     Running   0          12d
serving-az3-rt-1                       1/1     Running   0          8d
serving-az3-batch-0                    0/1     CrashLoopBackOff  5   2h
model-shard-az3-3                      1/1     Running   0          3d
```
alex.chen: batch pod CrashLoopBackOff looks suspicious. grabbing logs from serving-az3-batch-0
jordan: logs show repeated KV cache migration failures then segfault in runtime: `segfault at 0x00000000 ip ...` Looks like CVM oom+corruption pattern.
sasha: could be memory pressure + heavy batch compaction. We recently rolled a kernel bump on az3 nodes last week though.
nate: I see increase in `eviction_rate` on az3 NVM caches around same time. Could be underlying host storage flaking causing persistent process failures.
alex.chen: good catch. Let's isolate: - move traffic off az3 into az2/az4 for affected routing policy - scale up fallback capacity on az2 - mark az3 pool as degraded so autoscaler pauses rebalances. Who can push traffic diversion?
jordan: I can update routing policy. Proposed quick diversion: add tag to az3-serving pool: `degraded=true` and then update smart-router weight from 0.4->0.1.
ops-coordinator: do we want full divert or partial? customer impact will be lower latency but potential capacity hit in az2/az4.
alex.chen: start with partial divert 75% away (weight 0.1 az3). If further errors continue, escalate to full divert. jordan — perform step and report.
jordan: doing now. `api call: POST /routing/policies/active -d {"pool_weights": {"az3":0.1, "az2":0.6, "az4":0.3}}`
pagerduty-bot: Notification: routing change detected for PID-83421.
jordan: changed. watching metric windows.
mira: after weight change, error rate in gen-text-v2 dropped from 12% -> 4.5% in 90s. queue depth down ~40%. Latency still slightly high on tails.
celine-srm: updating customers: "We’re seeing degraded performance in region (az3). Traffic is being rerouted and we expect partial mitigation within minutes. Will follow up with timeline."
ops-coordinator: status page note (draft): "Partial region degradation in az3: API errors affecting a subset of requests. Traffic being diverted to neighboring regions. No ETA for full recovery; engineering investigating root cause."
sasha: I want to be careful pausing autoscaler: if we pause it might mask underlying capacity scarcity. Suggest we set pool to drain mode for new allocations only.
alex.chen: agreed. set pool to `no_new_alloc` to avoid churn. jordan — can you set `no_new_alloc` on az3-serving?
jordan: `PUT /pools/az3-serving {"no_new_alloc": true}` — applied.
nate: I'm going to check the host-level logs for recent kernel messages, dmesg shows frequent iommu timeouts and blk errors on host-az3-07 over the past hour.
sasha: host-az3-07 is part of the batch job ring. If storage on that host is flaky, it could trigger kvcache thrash and cause process crashes.
alex.chen: isolate host-az3-07 from schedulers. nate, can you cordon it and request maintenance? We'll evacuate pods away.
nate: cordoning now: `kubectl cordon host-az3-07` — succeeds. Starting pod evictions.
pagerduty-bot: PID-83421 escalated to L2 after 8 minutes without full mitigation. L2: sasha notified.
sasha: ack. I’m jumping in. What’s the plan for pod replacement? If eviction tries to place pods back on same faulty host we loop. Need to update node selector to avoid host-az3-07 until fix.
jordan: scheduler already respects `unschedulable` nodes, evictions will prefer healthy nodes. Evictions in flight: 18 pods.
celine-srm: any estimate for customer impact window? I need to update SMT.
ops-coordinator: with diversion and cordon in place, visible customer error rates dropped ~70% for the impacted model. We'll keep status update every 15m.
alex.chen: next steps: - continue draining faulty host - look for core dumps on batch runtime to confirm segfault reason - validate disk IO and restart strategy - consider bringing up a replacement host from spare pool if host repairs expected >30m.
sasha: I’ll gather core dumps and start a debug container with gdb on latest crash. Also checking if the recent kernel bump could expose new bug in runtime.
mira: FYI, a smaller percentage of requests still get 5xx but mostly routing-related 502s due to transient proxy retries.
jordan: I've increased fallback capacity in az2 by adding 4 serving instances: `scale service serving-az2 4` — applied.
nate: host replacement tentatively available: spare-host-az3-12. Can provision as hot-swap. Would need 12m to boot and join cluster.
alex.chen: do it. Provision spare-host-az3-12, then migrate critical batch pods there.
nate: provisioning started. ETA ~12m.
pagerduty-bot: Reminder: SLA owner notification: ops@redwood.com.
celine-srm: message to top impacted customers posted in DM thread. Collecting affected request ids for post-incident.
ops-coordinator: small ask: can someone verify ML model state consistency after crashes? We want to avoid serving stale/partial KV shards.
sasha: checking model-shard-az3-* — most shards report healthy except `model-shard-az3-5` which failed leader election during crash window. I'm forcing a resync: `POST /shards/az3/5/resync`
alex.chen: good. After resync, run quick evals against golden prompts to ensure outputs stable. mira can run those.
mira: running evals... initial pass looks fine, no obvious hallucination spikes. I'll run more.
jordan: host replacement completed: spare-host-az3-12 joined cluster, pods scheduled. Initial health checks green. Evicted pods redistributed.
mira: after migration and routing diversion, global error rate back near baseline. az3 5xx at 0.8% now. Latency tails returning to normal.
sasha: I found core with null-deref in `cache_migrate()` and raised bug with runtime team. Seems to be a race under heavy eviction + compaction. Noted: revertable kernel module may mitigate but patch will be needed.
alex.chen: next operational steps: - keep pool weight low (0.1) for 30m while monitoring - mark incident as mitigated if no regressions in 30m - follow up with a postmortem and runtime bugfix.
pagerduty-bot: PID-83421 status: mitigated (partial) — assigned to alex.chen for follow-up.
celine-srm: sharing customer follow-up: "We routed traffic away from az3 to preserve availability; root cause appears to be a host storage/eviction cascade causing runtime crashes. We'll share a post-incident report with timelines and corrective actions."
nate: infra will schedule host-az3-07 maintenance and replace underlying disk. ETA for OS-level fix: 48h, with temporary host replacement in place.
ops-coordinator: FYI, leaving incident channel open for 2 hours for watch. Set reminders to review graphs in 15/30/60m.
mira: adding small monitoring query to alert if az3 error >1% for 5m.
sasha: filing bug RN-4521 against runtime with reproducible steps and core attached.
alex.chen: thanks all. great coordination. final note: we resolved customer-facing impact via routing diversion + host swap; follow-up actions: postmortem, runtime patch, longer-term host health checks.
ops-coordinator: closing PD loop: mark incident as mitigated in PD, continue watch.
pagerduty-bot: Incident PID-83421: acknowledged, mitigated, on-call closed the active page.
alex.chen: marking thread resolved for now. Please add anything else if you see regressions. :thumbsup:
